Name: Young Adult Wormhole Dragon
Information:
**Wormhole Dragons**

These deep-space dragons are a blight to ships that happen to encounter them, and a shadow looming in every debris belt and asteroid moving through exolunar space. They are predatory by nature, seeking anything that sparks their curiosity and destroying anything that gets between them and it. They are highly intelligent when it comes to reasoning and planning, but their isolation leaves them selfish and with a childish mentality, so much so that they don’t consider the effect they have on other creatures.

**Flippant Motivations.** A wormhole dragon is motivated entirely by a focus on breaking from its usual boring patterns: their life in exolunar space rarely holds surprises, and sometimes it can take decades for anything to come through their part of space. As a result, they seek out excitement and try to get the most out of toying with lesser creatures that catch their attention. They can be won over by those who promise them amusement or by people who strike them as fascinating, but they usually get bored with their arrangements and muses quickly. They may even betray allies of “lesser standing” in their boredom, hoping the resulting turmoil will be fun to navigate.

**Cosmic Predators.** Wormhole dragons are cunning hunters who lurk among rocks and meteors to patiently wait for prey to come to them. Utilizing their ability to warp and shift around space, they use hit-and-run tactics to injure their prey then retreat and plan their next move. They are more agile than most dragons, and exploit that for the purposes of overcoming the dangers of exolunar space.

Luckily, most wormhole dragons see the hunt as mere fun. They often keep their sustenance in their lairs and have set hunting grounds they warp between, so their “opportunistic” hunts are more often than not just a ploy to pass time. They may attack a spacefaring vessel until the excitement passes or it poses any moderate threat, then will warp away and leave it in disrepair.

**Planetary Tourists.** Occasionally, a wormhole dragon will choose to visit a populated planet and live for some time as a resident there. They will assume the form of a local creature and spend a human lifetime exploring and “window shopping” in their society. These stints of exploration are a hobby to them, which they gleefully indulge in to pass time. While ingratiated with a society, they will slowly find people and things they desire and lure them to a situation where they can warp them back to their lair, keeping them as possessions, servants, or concubines.

A wormhole dragon’s exit from such a “vacation” will usually involve revealing itself in the process of stealing something of great importance: a high ranking public servant, a landmark, an entire building or treasury, etc. To the dragon, taking people, places, and things doesn’t cause lasting damage to the world they come from; on the contrary, they see it as enriching their personal world contained in their lair, and see the acquisition of servants as inviting them into a paradise.

**Egocentric Tells.** A common reason for such a dragon being caught in a disguise is due to their consistent inability to recognize the cultures they insert themselves into as their own. Even if they live 100 years on a planet, they will still speak as though they were visiting and use language that separates “their world” from the one they’re inhabiting. Though not obvious at a glance, this behavior can raise suspicions.

**Quote**

“Humanoid forms come and go as needed, but the form of humans and astral elves are my favorites. They have a charming efficiency and elegance to them, and can pop up anywhere across the galaxy. As useful as they are appealing.”

traits.name: Sympathetic Warp
traits.description: When the dragon uses its teleport speed, any creature mounting it, or who is being grappled by/grappling the dragon directly teleports along with it. This does not end these grapples.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) piercing damage plus 5 (1d8) force damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.

actions.name: Inversion Wave (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The dragon creates an inverted gravity well that projects out from it in a 45-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Strength saving throw, taking 55 (10d10) force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Each creature who fails by 5 points or more is also pushed 20 feet back from the dragon and knocked prone.

actions.name: Wormhole (1/Week)
actions.description: The dragon produces the effects of the teleport spell. When it does it leaves a black hole-like spherical disturbance in space where it vanished, which fills the space it occupied. There is a 50% chance that the disturbance may collapse at the start of each of the dragon’s turns, sealing it. While it is present, any creature who ends their turn in the disturbance or enters it for the first time on their turn must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be teleported to the nearest unoccupied space in the same location the dragon teleported to.

bonus_actions.name: Change Shape
bonus_actions.description: The dragon transforms into any creature that is Medium, Small, or Tiny, while retaining its statistics (other than its size), though if it is Tiny it cannot use its Multiattack. This transformation ends if the dragon is reduced to 0 hit points.

options.name: Gravity Warp
options.description: The dragon creates a gravity well centered on a point it can see within 120 feet. Each creature (except the dragon) in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must succeed a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pulled toward that sphere’s center (they are moved up to half the sphere’s radius), and their movement speed is halved until the end of their next turn. The dragon may spend two Legendary Actions on this action, doubling the sphere’s radius to 60 feet.

options.name: Shimmer
options.description: The dragon teleports to an unoccupied space it can see within 30 feet.

options.name: Warping Strike (Costs 2 Actions)
options.description: The dragon targets up to six different creatures it can see within 60 feet and makes a single Claw attack. That attack warps through space and is applied against each target individually.

legendary_reactions.source_conversion_note: Converted from Legendary Resistance (2/Day) per standing formatting rule.
